review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the Path.Homotopic.Quotient simp lemmas in Mathlib/Topology/Homotopy/Path.lean and the downstream uses in FundamentalGroupoid/InducedMaps.lean, FundamentalGroup.lean and Topology/Homotopy/Lifting.lean. The Quotient lemmas `refl_trans`, `trans_refl`, `trans_symm`, `symm_trans` and `trans_assoc` carry sensible simp and grind attributes, with no loop and no conflicting orientation. `map_id`, `map_comp` and the `equiv` lemmas also look fine. The two findings are interface gaps, not defects in existing rules, and I have not run Lean. Whether `map_eq` is a safe simp lemma depends on how simp unifies `TopCat.ofHom f` with `πₘ` applications in practice. I have not tested that. Whether to bridge `≫` to `Quotient.trans` is a design choice. Making `comp_eq` simp as written would be risky, so I only suggest a narrower bridge.

findings.excerpt:
theorem map_eq {X Y : TopCat.{u}} {x₀ x₁ : X} (f : C(X, Y)) (p : Path.Homotopic.Quotient x₀ x₁) :
    (πₘ (TopCat.ofHom f)).map p = p.map f := rfl
findings.problem: `fundamentalGroupoidFunctor` has no `@[simps]` and its `obj` and `map` fields have no simp lemmas. `FundamentalGroupoid.map` does have them, via `@[simps]`. So `(πₘ (TopCat.ofHom f)).map p` has no simp path down to `Path.Homotopic.Quotient.map`. The bridge `map_eq` is a plain `rfl` theorem. The only downstream use is a manual `simp only [map_eq]` in InducedMaps.evalAt_eq.
findings.proposed_change: Mark `map_eq` as `@[simp]`, since its RHS `p.map f` is the normal form that the `@[simps]`-generated `FundamentalGroupoid.map_map` also produces. Alternatively, put `@[simps]` on `fundamentalGroupoidFunctor` and add a companion lemma for `.obj`. Then the `TopCat`-level functor and the `C(X,Y)`-level `map` share one canonical form, `Quotient.map p f`.
findings.benefit: Users working with `πₘ` get the same normal form as with `FundamentalGroupoid.map`. Files like InducedMaps no longer need to name `map_eq` in `simp only`, and `map_eq` can no longer be forgotten.

findings.excerpt: theorem comp_eq (x y z : FundamentalGroupoid X) (p : x ⟶ y) (q : y ⟶ z) : p ≫ q = p.trans q := rfl
findings.problem: The simp and grind lemmas `Quotient.refl_trans`, `trans_refl`, `trans_symm`, `symm_trans`, `trans_assoc` and `Quotient.mk_trans` are all stated in terms of `Quotient.trans` and `Quotient.refl`. Terms in the groupoid are written with `≫` and `𝟙`. Nothing in the simp set connects `fromPath (Quotient.trans a b)` to `fromPath a ≫ fromPath b`, or `fromPath (refl x)` to `𝟙 _`. `comp_eq` and `id_eq_path_refl` are not simp lemmas, and they rewrite in the direction away from the categorical normal form. They are used only through explicit `simp only [..., comp_eq, ...]` in InducedMaps. After `simp` rewrites with `mk_trans`, a goal that mixes `≫` with `Quotient.trans` can get stuck.
findings.proposed_change: Do not make `comp_eq` or `id_eq_path_refl` simp as stated, because that would turn `≫` into `Quotient.trans` and fight `Category.id_comp` and `Category.assoc`. Instead add simp lemmas in the other direction for the bridge, for example `fromPath (Path.Homotopic.Quotient.trans p q) = fromPath p ≫ fromPath q` and `fromPath (Path.Homotopic.Quotient.refl x) = 𝟙 (FundamentalGroupoid.mk x)`. Both would be `rfl` proofs. Then `≫` is the groupoid-level normal form, and the existing categorical simp lemmas apply after `mk_trans`.
findings.benefit: Simp reaches a canonical categorical form for paths viewed as groupoid morphisms, without manual `comp_eq`-style rewrites. It also avoids the two competing vocabularies, `Quotient.trans` and `≫`, in one goal.
